answer.original_source: NN, Inc. (company announcement, as relayed by finance.yahoo.com; the source record states no original announcement day)
answer.new_information: NN, Inc. announced in late June 2026 a liquid cooling production expansion for NVIDIA AI data center racks, adding 47 machine centers at its Wuxi, China plant. NN stated that 100% of the new capacity was pre-sold under multi-year, multi-product awards and targeted US$80–US$90 million of accretive new business in 2026. This is a supplier's own announced plan and statements, relayed by Yahoo on 2026-07-01, so it is party-stated, not verified. The text does not name the award-giving customer; the NVIDIA link comes from the article's framing, so the customer identity is unconfirmed. The article also reports NN's removal from the Russell Microcap Value Index, its narrative projections of about $485.5M revenue and $47.9M earnings by 2028, and an unnamed analysts' estimate of about $489.5M and $48.3M. These concern NN, not NVDA, and the analyst estimate is a rumour-tier item.
answer.reason: The identified origin is NN, Inc.'s own announcement, relayed by finance.yahoo.com. No catalog or matched claim exists, so this marks the first identified origin rather than corroboration. item:e2 restates the same pre-sold claim from the same relay and is not independent. The Russell removal, the NN revenue and earnings projections, and the unnamed analyst estimate have no connection to NVDA's business. The 2026 US$80–US$90M target is NN's new business, not NVDA's revenue, so it is not an NVDA annual quantity.
answer.independent_judgement: For NVDA, this is at most a weak, indirect supply-chain signal. NN is a supplier, and a supplier's revenue and capacity are not NVDA's revenue or orders. The text supports only NN's own claims that it added 47 machine centers and holds pre-sold multi-year awards for liquid cooling capacity. It does not establish that NVIDIA is the buyer of those awards, nor any NVDA volume, pricing, or timing. The article's framing of NVIDIA's Asia supply chain is an inference from the headline and is not confirmed by the supplied text. The new capacity could hint at continued data center rack cooling demand, but that link is conditional and not decision-relevant without an NVIDIA-side source. No catalog question carries this, and the remaining items are about NN or are rumour-tier, so no argument change is supported.
